questions.question: What is an indemnity clause?
questions.expected_answer: A general explanation (a contractual promise by one party to compensate the other for specified losses or liabilities), clearly labelled as general knowledge, not as Verified from the documents.
questions.answer_text: An indemnity clause is a contract provision in which one party agrees to compensate the other for losses, damages, or liabilities that arise from specified events or actions. It typically shifts the financial risk of certain claims from the indemnitee to the indemnitor. The clause may define the scope of covered losses, the circumstances triggering indemnification, and any limits or procedural requirements. Such clauses are common in commercial agreements to allocate risk between the parties.

questions.question: What is the difference between a mutual and a one-way non-disclosure agreement?
questions.expected_answer: A general explanation (mutual: both parties disclose and are bound; one-way: only one party discloses and only the recipient is bound), labelled as general knowledge.
questions.answer_text: A one‑way (or unilateral) non‑disclosure agreement obligates only the receiving party to keep the disclosing party’s information confidential, while the disclosing party has no reciprocal duty. A mutual (or bilateral) NDA imposes confidentiality obligations on both parties, each of whom may both disclose and receive protected information. In practice, a one‑way NDA is used when only one side is sharing sensitive data, whereas a mutual NDA is used when the parties will exchange confidential information with each other. The core difference is therefore who is bound by the confidentiality obligations.
questions.grounded_answer_text: INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT: The provided passages do not contain information defining or contrasting mutual and one-way non‑disclosure agreements.
questions.label: CORRECT_GENERAL
questions.note: Accurate mutual vs one-way explanation, labelled general knowledge.
